source: Working draft from project report; derived from 2021 AHA/ACC chest pain guideline Section 2.1. ALL ITEMS UNVERIFIED.

items.label: Onset and timing
items.description: Clinician establishes when the pain started and how it began.
example_questions: Did it come on suddenly or gradually?
items.guideline_ref: 2021 AHA/ACC/ASE/CHEST/SAEM/SCCT/SCMR Guideline for the Evaluation and Diagnosis of Chest Pain (Gulati et al.), Section 2.1 History, Table 3 (item-level content unchecked)
items.verification_note: Section 2.1 / Table 3 existence confirmed via ACC 'Guidelines Made Simple' summary; Table 3 content could not be read (primary text returned 403). Item NOT confirmed against the guideline.

items.label: Exertional pattern
items.description: Clinician asks whether the pain is brought on or worsened by exertion or relieved by rest.
example_questions: Does it happen when you walk or climb stairs?
items.guideline_ref: 2021 AHA/ACC/ASE/CHEST/SAEM/SCCT/SCMR Guideline for the Evaluation and Diagnosis of Chest Pain (Gulati et al.), Section 2.1 History, Table 3 (item-level content unchecked)

items.label: Radiation
items.description: Clinician asks whether pain spreads to the arm, jaw, neck or back.
example_questions: Does the pain travel anywhere, like your arm or jaw?

items.label: Sweating
items.description: Clinician asks about sweating (diaphoresis) with the pain.
example_questions: Do you break out in a sweat when it happens?

items.label: Shortness of breath
items.description: Clinician asks about shortness of breath with the pain.
example_questions: Are you short of breath when this happens?
items.guideline_ref: 2021 AHA/ACC/ASE/CHEST/SAEM/SCCT/SCMR Guideline for the Evaluation and Diagnosis of Chest Pain (Gulati et al.), Section 2.1 History, Table 3 (item-level content unchecked)
items.verification_note: Section 2.1 / Table 3 existence confirmed via ACC 'Guidelines Made Simple' summary; Table 3 content could not be read (primary text returned 403). Item NOT confirmed against the guideline. Shortness of breath as an accompanying symptom/anginal equivalent is supported at summary level (take-home messages, Sections 1.4.2 and 2.1.1).

items.label: Fainting
items.description: Clinician asks about fainting, near-fainting or lightheadedness.
example_questions: Have you passed out or felt like you might?

items.label: Family history
items.description: Clinician asks about heart disease in close relatives, especially early onset.
example_questions: Has anyone in your family had heart problems at a young age?

items.label: Risk factors
items.description: Clinician asks about cardiac risk factors: smoking, blood pressure, diabetes, cholesterol.
example_questions: Any history of high blood pressure, diabetes or high cholesterol?
